title: Isomorphisms descend along etale surjections
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $u:U\to X$ be a surjective etale morphism of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes, and let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a morphism of bounded
constructible complexes on $X$. If $Lu^*\varphi$ is an isomorphism,
then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The singleton family with member f is an etale cover: its sole map is etale and is surjective. Mathlib Scheme.ofArrows_mem_precoverage_iff gives membership in etalePrecoverage, and Scheme.etalePrecoverage_le_proetalePrecoverage gives the required pro-etale cover. This incorporates the finite-affine-refinement argument of the old plan, including the empty scheme.

For sheaves valued in modules over ULift A, the source-library ProEtale.upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction computes inverse image by localization restriction along the weakly etale f. The source-library ProEtale.isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction applies the sheaf equalizer axiom to the base changes of the singleton cover, and therefore detects invertibility of any sheaf morphism. These are the published localization comparison and cover-local inverse argument of the original steps 2 and 4; no geometric stalk conservativity is asserted.

proof.text: At the fixed finite ring A=P.Ring, sfIntrinsicPullback is definitionally the composite of the inverse realization equivalence at X, fixed-module upperStar, and the realization equivalence at U. Both equivalences reflect isomorphisms. The preceding step makes upperStar reflect isomorphisms, so the composite does too, by the composition instance. This uses the actual canonical coefficient realization in the definition, with no new coefficient identification or chosen module object.

proof.text: The intrinsic derived pullback is definitionally the exact functor sfIntrinsicPullback.mapDerivedCategory. For each integer n, mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso identifies the pullback of the n-th cohomology morphism with the n-th cohomology of the pulled-back morphism. The latter is invertible by the hypothesis and functorial preservation of isomorphisms. Reflection from step 3 gives invertibility of each original cohomology map. DerivedCategory.isIso_iff then gives invertibility of the ambient derived morphism.

proof.text: The inclusion of the full bounded constructible subcategory reflects isomorphisms. Its image of phi is definitionally phi.hom, proved invertible in step 4, so reflection yields IsIso phi. No constructibility-preservation hypothesis or bound on cohomology is used in the ambient argument.
